The patient's history of neurofibromatosis type 1 and multiple cutaneous neurofibromas also supports this diagnosis, as Malignant Peripheral Nerve Sheath Tumors are known to occur in patients with neurofibromatosis type 1.

However, the expression of S100 and neurofilaments is consistent with neurofibroma. The absence of pan-cytokeratin expression also supports this diagnosis, but the overall clinical and histological features are more suggestive of Malignant Peripheral Nerve Sheath Tumor.
